lessons.title: Print your first line and use variables.
lessons.explain: Variables hold values and print shows them. Python infers types, so there is no declaration step.
lessons.exercise: Store your age and favorite language in variables and print one sentence using both.
lessons.code:
# your first program
name = "coal"
print("hello,", name)
age = 17
print(age + 1)
lessons.solutionDiff:
age = 17

-# TODO: print one sentence using both
+print("I am", age, "and I love", lang)

lessons.title: Repeat work with for and while.
lessons.explain: A for loop walks over a sequence and while repeats until a condition fails. Indentation marks the loop body.
lessons.exercise: Print the multiplication table of 7, from 1 to 10.

lessons.title: Wrap logic in reusable functions.
lessons.explain: A function names a block of logic so you can reuse it. Parameters go in and return sends a value out.

lessons.title: Model things with classes.
lessons.explain: A class bundles data with the functions that use it. __init__ runs when you create an object and self is that object.
lessons.exercise: Add a method to Bot that counts how many times hi() has been called.
